messages:
Ravi (AE): FYI, Customer asked to pivot this POC — priority now is real-time similarity search + rerank with p95 latency target 150ms and timeline shortened to 2w. They explicitly want BYO KMS and conservative privacy controls. Can SE/infra weigh in on what's feasible and the cost delta? :eyes:
Anna (SE): Ok noted. Need to lock success criteria. From sales convo: 1) p95 end-to-end <150ms for top-3 responses, 2) match quality >= baseline on their eval set (we need their prompts), 3) BYO KMS + audit logs, 4) demo flow in 2w. Does that match? :thinking:
Ravi (AE): Correct. They're pushing hard on latency. They also said they can accept a small drop in relevance if cost/latency improves.
Maya (Infra): Short answer: 150ms p95 is tough on hosted general fleet for rerank+embed for 100ms query budgets. Options: dedicated pool in same region, smaller model variant for rerank (e.g., tiny-rerank), aggressive quantization + KV cache, or truncating context. Tradeoffs: quantization -> possible quality regressions; tiny model -> lower relevance but much faster.
Anna (SE): For the evals, can they share a ~500 prompt set (mix of short/long) so we can run quality and latency together? We should run both 'cold' and 'warm' KV cache scenarios. Also propose these success metric definitions: "p95 end-to-end measured in our harness", "R@10 >= X on their eval".
Sam (SRE): Security note: BYO KMS is supported only on Private and Dedicated deployments. Hosted API can't bind customer KMS. If BYO KMS is a hard requirement, we need Dedicated or Private (ops + procurement). Also BYO KMS adds ~2–3 business days for key provisioning and test vector signing.
Emily (PM): Pricing implications: Dedicated short-term commit (2w trial) is possible but requires an estimate. Can infra give rough delta per 100k queries/day for dedicated vs hosted? We need that to set expectations with customer.
Maya (Infra): Rough back-of-envelope: if we serve rerank + embedding at target latency with a small dedicated GPU cluster (4x A10s for bursty 2w POC), expected incremental infra cost ~ $9k–$14k for the period (depends on region and sustained qps). With quantization+model-change we could get to 150ms with 2x A10s -> ~$5k. These are infra-only ballparks.
Anna (SE): Notes on tests — here's a tiny perf harness snippet we can run against their sample prompts (will run in our staging):
```
# py perf loop
import time, requests
for q in sample_prompts:
    t0 = time.time()
    r = requests.post(url, json={"prompt": q, "max_tokens": 64})
    print((time.time()-t0)*1000)
```
Run both cold (restart runtime) and warm (same session) to see KV cache benefits.
Ravi (AE): Customer also asked about embedding storage — they want results persisted in their DB and rerank to be done in-memory. Any concerns?
Maya (Infra): That pattern is fine. For 150ms rerank consider doing embedding lookup in Redis with local CPU ranking for top-K then rerank with model on only top-20 candidates to save time. That reduces infer token work.
Sam (SRE): For audit/compliance: enabling KMS + audit logs requires a Private control plane or Dedicated with audit forwarding set up. We'll need SOC artifacts and an updated security questionnaire entry. Anna, can you collect the exact questionnaire fields they flagged?
Anna (SE): I'll pull the questionnaire and highlight the BYO KMS + data residency rows. Also need to ask for sample eval set and expected QPS.
Emily (PM): Proposed success criteria to confirm with customer and sign-off: 1) p95 end-to-end <=150ms (measured on our harness in their region), 2) Eval quality >= baseline (we'll define metric after we get their evals), 3) BYO KMS + audit logs validated, 4) runbook for failover to fallback model under high latency. If any of these fail, provide a mitigation plan.
Ravi (AE): I'll ask them to share the 500 prompts and target baseline numbers. Also will confirm whether BYO KMS is mandatory or just preferred.
Anna (SE): If BYO KMS mandatory -> plan = Dedicated -> infra estimate + procurement lead time (2–3 days). If optional -> we can try hosted + model/quantization tweaks to hit latency faster.
Maya (Infra): Quick checklist for team before demo:
- get eval set (500 items)
- run warm/cold perf with sample harness
- test tiny-rerank + top-K truncation
- quantify quality delta vs baseline
- provide infra cost delta and commit options
Sam (SRE): I'll draft the minimal audit log steps + KMS checklist and post it in this thread. ops-bot, tag:deploy?
ops-bot: Acknowledged. Drafting KMS/Audit checklist and will attach as soon as ready.
Ravi (AE): Great. Can we aim to have the perf numbers + cost delta by EOD Tuesday? We promised them a timeline estimate. :thumbsup:
Anna (SE): Will try. If they push for 2w end-to-end, we should be conservative and propose a 2-phase POC: Phase 1 (1w): validate quality and infra approach with smaller dataset; Phase 2 (1w): full perf tuning and final demo. That reduces risk.
Emily (PM): Agree. I'll prepare a short slide for execs summarizing tradeoffs (cost vs latency vs quality) that Ravi can share.
Maya (Infra): One more technical callout: network egress from their DB -> our runtimes may add ~10–30ms depending on region. Factor that into p95 budget.
Ravi (AE): Noted. I'll push for their region + expected QPS. Thanks all — I will update thread with eval set when they share.
Anna (SE): :thumbsup: closing loop — will start a staging run as soon as evals arrive.
ops-bot: Checklist draft uploaded: /internal/kms-audit-checklist/1801234567 (ops only).
